correctness.rationale: All quantifiers and boundaries specified: initial normalized Lebesgue, finite arbitrary deterministic schedule, first true intervention only. Full tent sign symbols are iid fair bits, and u=1/2 plateau is exactly the RL test at two successive shifted symbols off a null set. Runs test disjoint digit blocks. RL avoidance in length l+1 has exactly l+2 words, giving p_l; p_a p_b-p_(a+b)=ab/2^(a+b+2)>0 proves min/r optimality. Concavity of log(l+2) yields exact balanced max and equality; infinite controls use (3/4)^k upper bound. Standalone exact-rational checker verified all 510 schedules through horizon 8 and 36 k/N extrema; these are supporting checks, not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: A natural practical/statistical question left by time-dependent simple-limiter control is how to allocate a fixed number of interventions within a finite horizon. The result supplies a universal exact run decomposition and both globally sharp schedule extrema, not just an isolated numerical probability; clustering vs spacing changes non-intervention probabilities by an exponential factor 2(3/2)^k/(k+2) when spacing is feasible. It also proves almost-sure first activation for arbitrarily sparse infinite patterns. The parameter u=1/2 is canonically motivated by an exact two-symbol central plateau, not arbitrary enumeration; the result does not claim post-activation attractor control.
